flags.subject: Hotspawn counts differ from the parseable open slate
flags.detail: The page header says "131 matches this week"; the ng-state payload yields 388 fixtures, of which 262 have a lock time in the future. Weekly counts include fixtures from other titles and rows already locked; the fixtures table is the authoritative list and is complete for the payload.

flags.subject: 114 Hotspawn rows are scheduled in the past but still listed as scheduled
flags.detail: These rows carry a scheduled start months before this capture and no bookmaker still prices them; they are listed here for completeness but are not part of the pickable slate and get no line or pick.

flags.subject: 233 open fixtures have no external market line
flags.detail: No price could be read from the sources this run (a source that returns an error or serves no odds table is recorded as a refusal). Those rows show the price as blank, exactly as read — nothing is estimated.

flags.subject: 234 open fixtures have no originated line
flags.detail: At least one team in the fixture has no row with an exact name match in the HLTV ranking or Valve's standings, so no rating-based probability is invented for it.

flags.subject: 230 open fixtures have no pick at all
flags.detail: Neither a market line nor an official rating pair is available for these rows, so they are published blank with this flag rather than filled in.

flags.subject: 9 fixtures carry a price another session read, not re-read here
flags.detail: For these rows the CI run could not reach a bookmaker page (HTTP 403 is recorded in the provenance log) and this session did not read that fixture's own page, so the headline price is the newest source-linked reading already published in this repository, with the reading session, its capture time and its page URL shown on the row. Prices move: treat these as the older reading they are, and check the linked page before relying on them.

flags.subject: 8 fixtures were priced from this session's own page reading
flags.detail: EGamersWorld refuses the CI runner (HTTP 403) but serves the project's fetch service, so these prices were read by the session at the times recorded per row, with the page URL on every row. The scheduled CI job keeps trying the same pages and will replace these rows with its own fresh readings whenever the host serves it again.

flags.subject: 5 fixtures where the market price and our own rating line disagree
flags.detail: For these rows the external bookmaker price and the official-rating model point at different winners. The pick stays with the market price (it is the observable market view), the model's side is shown next to it, and both source links are on the row. A disagreement is information, not an error: it says the two independent methods are not telling the same story here.

flags.subject: Hotspawn's printed wall-clock time is not a reliable UTC value
flags.detail: The printed time next to a match is rendered for the viewer, and this project's own readings show the same fixture printed as both UTC and UTC-4 on the same pages in different sessions, while the ticker ("Locks in ...") and the ng-state epoch always agree. Every time in slate/data comes from the ng-state epoch, never from the printed text.

flags.subject: No Hotspawn crowd percentage is used as a probability
flags.detail: The crowd "% picked" values are readable from the payload. They are copied into fixtures.csv under column names ending in _audit_only for transparency, and no build step reads those columns. Every probability on the site comes from an external bookmaker price, from our own official-rating model, or is blank.
